title: RideWay: Benchmarking Efficient Task Completion for Tool-Using Language Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.17985v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI agents are usually evaluated by whether they complete a task. In interactive service settings, a successful agent can still frustrate users by asking repeated questions, performing redundant searches, or making avoidable revisions. We introduce RideWay, an efficiency-centered benchmark for ridehailing agents in a stateful tool-calling environment, together with Efficiency Utility, a success-gated metric that discounts successful trajectories for excess tool calls and user-facing turns relative to task-specific reference effort. Human paired preferences calibrate the relative penalties, reflecting an aggregate service-workflow trade-off: extra dialogue often creates visible friction, whereas extra tool use can sometimes verify constraints or preserve user intent. Across 58 tasks and 24 models, the fitted penalty for excess turns is about twice that for excess tool calls. On task-disjoint held-out preferences, Efficiency Utility achieve

translated_title: RideWay：面向工具使用型语言代理的高效任务完成基准测试
translated_abstract: AI智能体通常以是否完成任务作为评估标准。然而在交互式服务场景中，一个“成功”的智能体仍可能通过重复提问、执行冗余搜索或进行可避免的修改而使用户感到不满。我们提出了RideWay，一个以效率为中心的网约车智能体基准测试，运行在有状态的工具调用环境中；同时提出“效率效用”，这是一种以成功为门控的指标，它以任务特定的参考工作量为基准，对成功轨迹中多余的工具调用和面向用户的对话轮次进行折扣。人类配对偏好用于校准相对惩罚系数，反映了服务工作流的整体权衡：额外的对话往往造成明显的摩擦，而额外的工具调用有时可用于验证约束条件或保留用户意图。在58个任务和24个模型上的实验表明，多余对话轮次的拟合惩罚约为多余工具调用惩罚的两倍。在与任务无关的留出偏好数据上，效率效用达到……
tldr: 该论文提出RideWay网约车智能体效率基准与“效率效用”指标，利用人类配对偏好校准惩罚机制，发现多余对话轮次的代价约为多余工具调用代价的两倍，从而推动从“仅看任务成败”向“衡量服务效率”的智能体评估范式转变。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces RideWay, an efficiency-centered benchmark for ridehailing agents in a stateful tool-calling environment, and Efficiency Utility, a success-gated metric calibrated by human paired preferences, showing that excess dialogue turns incur roughly twice the penalty of excess tool calls.
